title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Meat

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and meat is a home recipe that combines whole‑grain pasta, a flavorful tomato‑based sauce, and tender meat. The dish offers a balanced mix of complex carbohydrates, protein, and beneficial vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta provides more fiber and micronutrients than regular white pasta.
Tomato sauce made from fresh tomatoes is rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that supports heart health.
Tomatoes retain a high amount of vitamin C when the sauce is not overcooked.
Lean beef or turkey is commonly used, reducing saturated fat content.
Homemade sauce lets you control salt and sugar levels, making the meal healthier.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta supplies dietary fiber that aids digestion and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Meat adds complete protein necessary for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce contain lycopene, which may reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and certain cancers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the whole grain pasta and meat provide B1, B3, and B6 vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish provides iron from meat and magnesium from whole grains, important for blood formation and nerve function.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should use a gluten‑free alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce can be salty; monitor added salt to keep sodium intake moderate.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Using fatty cuts of meat can increase saturated fat; opt for lean cuts whenever possible.

items.title: Acidity of tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes may aggravate acid reflux in some people; reduce sauce amount if needed.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Cook whole grain pasta until al dente. Sauté finely chopped meat until browned, then add onion, garlic, and tomatoes; simmer 15‑20 minutes, seasoning with basil, oregano, salt, and pepper. Toss the pasta with the sauce, serve hot, and optionally garnish with grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared pasta in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze for up to 2 months after cooling, using freezer‑safe bags.
